headline: NetBSD 11.0 Released After Significant Delays, Addresses Security Concerns
summary: The NetBSD project has officially released version 11.0, overcoming delays and acknowledging ongoing security issues, with a focus on transparency.
details: The NetBSD project has announced the official release of NetBSD 11.0, marking a significant milestone after an extended development period. Users can now download installation images for various architectures, with specific instructions available for ARM-based devices utilizing U-Boot.

This release comes with a candid acknowledgment of the increasing number of security issues, partly attributed to the rise of AI tools. Rather than further delaying the release, the NetBSD team has opted for transparency regarding known vulnerabilities, with plans to address them in the upcoming 11.1 release.

The development team highlighted that the release process has been streamlined and automated, but manual intervention and network transfer times for all platforms still contribute to the overall timeline. Release candidates were provided to allow users ample time for testing.

Specific open security-related issues include potential privilege escalation via /dev/hdaudio and remotely triggerable null pointer dereferences in ipfilter, though the latter is not included in released kernels by default. A use-after-free vulnerability in pf's fragment reassembly was also noted, with pf being deprecated.

All outstanding security pull requests are slated for inclusion in the upcoming NetBSD 11.1 release, which the project is targeting for release within the next two months. This approach prioritizes getting the stable version out while actively working on addressing newly reported vulnerabilities.
caption:

headline_marked: [[I ♥ RSS]] launches a new directory for RSS enthusiasts
headline: I ♥ RSS launches a new directory for RSS enthusiasts
summary: Andrew Shell has launched a directory for people who love RSS, featuring a live blogroll powered by FeedLand. Submit your website to join the community.
details: Andrew Shell, a Senior Software Engineer, has launched a new website called I ♥ RSS. The platform serves as a directory for individuals passionate about the RSS feed technology.

The directory already features Shell's own website and showcases a live blogroll on its homepage, which is powered by FeedLand. This feature provides a dynamic view of updated content from participating sites.

Shell encourages fellow RSS enthusiasts to visit the site and submit their own websites to be included in the growing directory. The initiative aims to foster a community around the continued use and appreciation of RSS.
